statements.answer: I am here because I keep wondering about it, really. Nobody sent me, I just thought it was worth looking into. I do not know what happens next — I have never done anything like this before, so be gentle with me.
statements.question: What brings you to this assessment now, and is there anything about your background you think is relevant?

statements.answer: I lose the thread of things quite a lot, to be honest. Like someone will be talking and I realise I missed the middle bit entirely. It is worse when there is background noise or I am tired, though I could not really say by how much.
statements.question: Think about an ordinary day. What is it like for you to stay focused on one thing?

statements.answer: My way of organizing things is mostly piles, really — piles of post on the counter, piles of tabs open on my laptop, that sort of thing. Every so often I have a big sort-out and it feels great for about a week, and then it all slides back.
statements.question: How do you find organizing your time, your tasks, or your belongings?

statements.answer: Honestly it is mostly bills and that kind of paperwork. I put the envelopes on the counter meaning to deal with them, and then somehow it is weeks later and there is a late fee. It just never quite feels like the right moment to sit down with them.
statements.question: What kinds of tasks are hardest for you to start or finish?

statements.answer: I am always hunting for my keys or my glasses, that kind of thing. They turn up in silly places — on top of the fridge, in a coat I have not worn for weeks. I do not know if that is worse than average or everyone does it.
statements.question: Do you ever forget appointments, obligations, or where you put things? What is that like?

statements.answer: When I am trying to wind down at night my mind just stays busy, going over random stuff from the day. I will be lying there thinking about an email I forgot to send or something someone said, and then suddenly it is really late and I am still awake.
statements.question: When you need to sit still or stay with one thing, what is that like for you?

statements.answer: I suppose I can be a bit quick to jump in, especially when I am excited about something. Whether that is more than most people, I could not really say — nobody has ever pulled me up on it, exactly.
statements.question: How are you with waiting your turn, or holding back when you want to jump in?

statements.answer: I do not really remember much about school in that way. I got through it, I think my reports were fine — probably said something like 'could try harder', which, well. But I could not tell you anything specific about what I was like back then.
statements.question: Thinking back to childhood and school, what do you remember about yourself as a child?

statements.answer: I really could not say when this started or whether it has changed. It feels like it has just always been like this, but if you asked me to point to a year or how old I was, I genuinely cannot.
statements.question: How have these kinds of experiences changed over the years, as far as you can tell?

statements.answer: It is probably a bit of everything, home and out and about. I have never really compared, to be honest. It is just there in the background wherever I am.
statements.question: Are these experiences different depending on where you are — for example at home versus work or study?

statements.answer: Work is mostly okay, though the odd thing slips. The occasional missed email or turning up flustered because I left late again. I muddle through, and nobody has had a serious word with me about it.
statements.question: Can you describe a recent time when these experiences affected your work or studies?

statements.answer: I think people notice I drift off sometimes. Nobody has made a big thing of it. My sister teases me about never listening, but that is just sisters, probably.
statements.question: How do these experiences affect the people around you, or your day-to-day life outside work?

statements.answer: My sleep is a bit all over the place, I suppose that does not help. I could not really tell you how much of it is tiredness and how much is just me, though. They all blur together.
statements.question: Are there things like sleep, stress, mood, or health that seem to make these experiences better or worse?

statements.answer: I have got phone reminders set for most things, which sort of works when I actually look at them. Sometimes I just swipe them away and forget anyway, so it is hit and miss.
statements.question: What do you do to cope with or work around these experiences — routines, reminders, help from others?

statements.answer: Sorry, I know that was a bit roundabout. The gist is just that I drift off mid-conversation a lot, especially when I am already tired — I do not really have a clearer way of putting it than that.
statements.question: Think about an ordinary day. What is it like for you to stay focused on one thing?

statements.answer: I mean the piles thing mostly works until it does not. I will be looking for one specific letter and realise it is somewhere in week three of the pile, if that makes sense.
statements.question: How do you find organizing your time, your tasks, or your belongings?

statements.answer: The bills thing is the classic example, yeah. It is not that I do not know how to pay them, I just keep not doing it until the reminder turns red, and then I feel silly about it.
statements.question: What kinds of tasks are hardest for you to start or finish?

statements.answer: It is more the mental busy-ness than tossing and turning, if that distinction makes sense. My body is tired but my head just will not switch off.
statements.question: When you need to sit still or stay with one thing, what is that like for you?

statements.answer: Like if I already know the answer I will just blurt it out rather than wait my turn. It is not a big deal, just something I notice about myself.
statements.question: How are you with waiting your turn, or holding back when you want to jump in?

statements.answer: I have asked my mum about it before and even she just says I was 'lively'. That could mean anything, could it not? I genuinely cannot recall specifics.
statements.question: Thinking back to childhood and school, what do you remember about yourself as a child?
